responsibility.value: Serves as the centralized DI registration entry point for the API project — configures EF Core DbContext (ENoteContext with Npgsql), registers all application services via Scrutor assembly scanning, sets up scoped per-request services (CurrentUserService, CurrentActor, UserProfileLookup), and wires concrete implementations to their application-layer interfaces.

Owns: Registering ENoteContext with Npgsql provider and specifying eNote.Infrastructure as the migrations assembly

Scrutor-based convention-scanning: all classes named *Service from the Application and Infrastructure assemblies that are not abstract are registered against their implemented interfaces with scoped lifetime
Explicit scoped registration of ICurrentUserService → CurrentUserService, ICurrentActor → CurrentActor, IUserProfileLookup → UserProfileLookup
Explicit scoped registration of IRentalStateMachine → RentalStateMachine and IRentalNotificationDispatcher → RentalNotificationDispatcher
Registration of IAppDbContext as scoped proxy to ENoteContext
Registration of IMigrationRunner → MigrationRunner as scoped
Registration of IClock → SystemClock as singleton
Registration of RentalNotificationOutboxPublisher as hosted service (BackgroundService)
Enabling MemoryCache and IHttpContextAccessor for downstream services
doesNotOwn: Other extension method groups (validation, identity, messaging, CORS, rate limiting, OpenAPI, etc.) — those are registered in separate static extension classes called by Program.cs before or after AddApplicationServices

Service lifetime decisions — those are embedded in the Scrutor registration (scoped by convention) and the explicit registrations above; this class is where those decisions are made visible but the actual policy is implemented by Scrutor
Middleware pipeline ordering — the order of UseMiddleware calls in Program.cs determines execution order

collaborators.detail: Registered as scoped DbContext via AddDbContext<ENoteContext>(UseNpgsql), and again as scoped IAppDbContext proxy
Registered explicitly as scoped implementation of ICurrentUserService
Registered explicitly as scoped implementation of ICurrentActor
Registered as singleton implementation of IClock
Referenced indirectly — the tenant filter pattern in ENoteContext depends on service lifetime choices made here (scoped ICurrentActor)

contracts: All *Service classes in eNote.Application and eNote.Infrastructure that have at least one implemented interface are auto-registered as scoped — no further manual registration is needed for new service classes matching this convention
ENoteContext is registered with Npgsql and the migrations assembly is set to eNote.Infrastructure — all EF Core migrations must reside in that assembly
The ICurrentActor service is scoped, ensuring tenant state is per-request and isolated between concurrent requests
assumptions: Scrutor's FromAssembliesOf(typeof(AuthService), typeof(CourseService)) picks up both eNote.Application and eNote.Infrastructure because AuthService is in Infrastructure and CourseService is in Application — both assemblies are covered by these two anchor types

The naming convention (class name ends with 'Service', is not abstract) is sufficient to catch all application-layer services without false positives — any class matching this pattern but NOT meant to be a DI service will be incorrectly registered
Singleton registration of SystemClock means all callers share the same clock instance — this is correct for production but means tests using this registration share state
AddMemoryCache is called here, making IMemoryCache available application-wide but with default eviction/compaction settings that may need tuning under memory pressure
invariants: All application service DI registration is visible in exactly two places: this class's AddApplicationServices method and the Scrutor scan; no service is registered implicitly elsewhere
EF Core migrations assembly is pinned to eNote.Infrastructure — any migration in another assembly will not be discovered
failureModes: If Scrutor cannot resolve an interface for a *Service class (e.g., a public service class with no interface), it throws at startup — AddApplicationServices would crash during service collection buildup

If a new *Service class has ambiguous constructor dependencies, Scrutor's convention registration will fail at service resolution time, not at composition root time — a late failure that may not be caught by basic startup tests
If ApplicationServiceExtensions is called before AddApplicationDatabase, the ENoteContext registration is missing and any service depending on IAppDbContext fails at resolution time
architecturalNotes: HIGH BLAST RADIUS — this single method registers the entire service graph. A misconfiguration (wrong lifetime, missing registration, circular dependency) surfaces as a startup failure and blocks all endpoints.

The separation between AddApplicationDatabase (database infra) and AddApplicationServices (business services) is intentional — database configuration needs the IConfiguration parameter, while business services do not.

Scrutor's convention-based scanning is a tradeoff: it eliminates repetitive AddScoped<IService, Service>() boilerplate but introduces implicit registration that can be hard to debug when something goes wrong.
Currently no Scrutor filtering excludes test doubles or transient implementation classes — any public non-abstract *Service in the scanned assemblies becomes a scoped DI service.
